content: 1. Emtricitabine levels may increase when co-administered with adefovir due to competition for renal clearance. Close monitoring is required, and caution should be exercised. Drugs that impair renal function or compete for active tubular secretion can elevate serum concentrations of emtricitabine. 2. Co-administration of emtricitabine and atazanavir increases the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Patients should be monitored closely, and caution is advised. 3. Emtricitabine should not be used with atidarsagene autotemcel due to potential interference with the manufacturing of the cellular therapy. Antiretroviral therapy (ART) should be discontinued at least one month before cell mobilization and during the elimination period of the drugs. 4. Emtricitabine and betibeglogene autotemcel should not be co-administered. ARTs should be stopped at least one month before mobilization and until all apheresis cycles are completed, as ARTs may interfere with the manufacturing of apheresis-derived cells. 5. Co-administration of emtricitabine and celecoxib may lead to increased drug levels due to reduced renal clearance. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. Toxicity may occur when emtricitabine is combined with drugs primarily excreted via glomerular filtration or active tubular secretion, including high-dose or multiple-dose NSAIDs. Alternatives to NSAIDs should be considered. 6. Cidofovir increases emtricitabine levels by competing for renal clearance. Caution and close monitoring are required. 7. Co-administration of emtricitabine and diclofenac may increase the levels of both drugs due to reduced renal clearance. Therapy should be adjusted, and close monitoring is necessary. Toxicity may result from combining emtricitabine with drugs excreted via glomerular filtration or active tubular secretion, including high-dose or multiple-dose NSAIDs. Alternatives to NSAIDs should be considered. 8. Co-administration of emtricitabine and diflunisal may increase the levels of both drugs due to reduced renal clearance. Therapy should be adjusted, and close monitoring is necessary. Toxicity may result from combining emtricitabine with drugs excreted via glomerular filtration or active tubular secretion, including high-dose or multiple-dose NSAIDs. Alternatives to NSAIDs should be considered. 9. Efavirenz and emtricitabine increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome when co-administered. Patients should be monitored closely, and caution is advised. 10. Emtricitabine should not be used with elivaldogene autotemcel due to potential interference with stem cell mobilization. ARTs should be discontinued at least one month before initiating stem cell mobilization therapy and during the elimination period of the drugs. 11. Emtricitabine should not be co-administered with elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF, as this combination is a complete regimen for HIV and should not be combined with other antiretrovirals. 12. Co-administration of emtricitabine and enfuvirtide increases the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Patients should be monitored closely, and caution is advised. 13. Co-administration of emtricitabine and etodolac may increase the levels of both drugs due to reduced renal clearance. Therapy should be adjusted, and close monitoring is necessary. Toxicity may result from combining emtricitabine with drugs excreted via glomerular filtration or active tubular secretion, including high-dose or multiple-dose NSAIDs. Alternatives to NSAIDs should be considered. 14. Co-administration of emtricitabine and fenoprofen may increase the levels of both drugs due to reduced renal clearance. Therapy should be adjusted, and close monitoring is necessary. Toxicity may result from combining emtricitabine with drugs excreted via glomerular filtration or active tubular secretion, including high-dose or multiple-dose NSAIDs. Toxicity may result from combining emtricitabine with drugs excreted via glomerular filtration or active tubular secretion, including high-dose or multiple-dose NSAIDs. Alternatives to NSAIDs should be considered. 16. Co-administration of emtricitabine and fosamprenavir increases the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Patients should be monitored closely, and caution is advised. 17. Ganciclovir increases emtricitabine levels through pharmacodynamic synergy, leading to an increased risk of hematologic toxicity. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. Alternatives should be considered if available. 18. Co-administration of emtricitabine and ibuprofen may increase the levels of both drugs due to reduced renal clearance. Therapy should be adjusted, and close monitoring is necessary. Therapy should be adjusted, and close monitoring is necessary. Toxicity may result from combining emtricitabine with drugs excreted via glomerular filtration or active tubular secretion, including high-dose or multiple-dose NSAIDs. Alternatives to NSAIDs should be considered. 22. Emtricitabine and lamivudine should not be co-administered due to therapeutic duplication and an increased risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Products containing these drugs should be avoided. 23. Co-administration of emtricitabine and lovotibeglogene autotemcel is not recommended. ARTs should be discontinued at least one month before mobilization and until all apheresis cycles are completed. Long-acting ARTs may require a longer discontinuation period. 24. Patients should be monitored closely, and caution is advised. 29. Co-administration of emtricitabine and nevirapine increases the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Patients should be monitored closely, and caution is advised. 30. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir may increase emtricitabine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. 31. Orlistat may decrease emtricitabine levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Loss of virological control has been reported in HIV-infected patients taking orlistat. HIV RNA levels should be monitored frequently, and orlistat should be discontinued if an increased viral load is confirmed. 32. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. Alternatives should be considered if available. 35. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 41. Valacyclovir increases emtricitabine levels by competing for renal clearance. Caution and close monitoring are required. 42. Valganciclovir increases emtricitabine levels through pharmacodynamic synergy, leading to an increased risk of hematologic toxicity. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. Alternatives should be considered if available. 43. Co-administration of emtricitabine and zidovudine increases the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Patients should be monitored closely, and caution is advised. 44. HIV-infected mothers are advised not to breastfeed to prevent postnatal transmission of HIV. Emtricitabine has been detected in human breast milk, but its effects on milk production or the breastfed child are unknown. Breastfeeding should be avoided due to the potential for HIV transmission, viral resistance, and adverse reactions in the infant.
